Africa’s energy story is not only about closing an access gap. It is about what access makes possible.
 
As we look towards 2030, this is one of the questions I believe deserves far greater attention. More than 560 million people across Sub-Saharan Africa still live without electricity, while around 970 million lack access to clean cooking. Yet Africa also holds immense potential: 60 per cent of the world’s best solar resources, over 30 per cent of known critical mineral reserves, growing digital capabilities and a new generation of entrepreneurs ready to build.
 
The challenge is to connect these strengths to delivery.
 
On Wednesday, 15 July, I will be speaking at the High-level Political Forum side event, From Evidence to Action: Accelerating Energy Access and Just Transitions in Africa, at the Permanent Representation of Nigeria to the United Nations in New York.
 
I look forward to discussing how we can accelerate a just energy transition that expands access, powers businesses, strengthens essential services and creates jobs, while using evidence, AI, geospatial analytics and real-time data to target finance, track progress and scale solutions faster.
 
Africa does not lack energy potential. What is needed now is the ability to translate that potential into results that people can see and feel in their daily lives.
 
📅Date: Wednesday, 15 July 2026


🕘Time: 9:00–10:30 AM EDT


📍Venue: Permanent Representation of Nigeria to the United Nations, 828 Second Avenue, 21st Floor, New York
 
I look forward to contributing to this timely conversation and reflecting on how we can turn evidence into action, and energy access into opportunity.
